subject: FinTechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fintechco.com>, Jane Park <jane.park@fintechco.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: FinTechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP

Hi Tom / Jane,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier - appreciate you walking us through the payment-routing flow. Per our conversation, I pulled together a concise performance/SLO checklist and next steps (MAP) so we can validate fit on latency and throughput before procurement. See key items below and attached checklist + load-test plan.

Quick summary of your stated targets from the demo:
- P95 latency (inference only): <= 120ms for single-request streaming responses
- Sustained throughput: 200 req/s for short prompts (~60 tokens) across 10 concurrent workers
- Peak concurrency: 500 concurrent users (bursty traffic) with acceptable degradation policy
- Streaming: chunked token streaming to client, max initial token latency <= 80ms

Action items (proposed MAP):
1) Redwood to run a 2-hour smoke load test in our sandbox against a pinned model variant - provide results (latency histogram, error rate, token cost). (Owner: Redwood - Aditya)
2) FinTechCo to provide a representative 1k prompt sample + message size distribution. (Owner: FinTechCo - Tom)
3) Agree on degradation policy: fallback to smaller/model-quantized variant when latency breach > 5% over 15m window. (Owner: joint)
4) Procurement readiness: share SLO summary and SLA redlines for procurement review. (Owner: FinTechCo / Redwood legal)

Attachments: slo-checklist.pdf, load-test-plan.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4 (link attached)

If the targets above look right, I'll schedule the sandbox load run for early next week and loop in Rishi (performance lead) to interpret results.

Thanks - looking forward to next steps.


Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

From: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Jane Park <jane.park@fintechco.com>
Date: Wed, 28 Apr 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP

Thanks Marissa - this looks great and matches what we discussed. A few clarifications from our side:

- P95 target: the 120ms is for inference time only (we'll add ~20ms network overhead on our side). Can you confirm instrumentation will separate model inference vs. network?
- Throughput: the 200 req/s is our steady-state per-region expectation; global peak could be higher (we estimate up to 350 req/s across regions).
- Streaming: very important - we need chunked streaming for progressive rendering in our UI. Initial token latency is critical (users judge perceived latency on first token).

We'll attach a sample prompt set by EOD. Procurement will want the SLA summary once we have the test results.

Also: can you do a brief run with quantized model variant (int8) to show cost/latency tradeoffs? That will help our cost evaluation.

Thanks - Tom
Tom Ellis
VP Product, FinTechCo
tom.ellis@fintechco.com | +1 (617) 555-0199

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fintechco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 29 Apr 2027 08:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FinTechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP

Tom - thanks for the quick reply and the clarity. A few notes from the infra side: 

- Instrumentation: yes - we'll provide per-request timing breakdown (gateway, queuing, model inference, token-emit latency). We'll run tests with both wall-clock and model-internal timestamps so you can separate network overhead.
- Load test plan: I'll run the sandbox job with both FP16 and int8 quantized variants. Deliverables: latency histograms (P50/P90/P95/P99), tail-latency traces, throughput curves, and cost-per-1M-tokens estimate.
- Streaming validation: we'll run a separate streaming test that measures time-to-first-token and average chunk intervals. We'll also validate against your client render cadence (if you can share the client chunk size expectations).

Proposed schedule:
- Thu 29 Apr: FinTechCo shares prompt set + client chunking expectations (Tom)
- Mon 3 May 09:00 PT: Redwood runs 2-hour steady-state test (200 req/s) + 30m spike test to 500 concurrency.
- Tue 4 May: Redwood shares raw results and a one-page SLO summary.

I've attached the load-test-plan.xlsx - simple checklist and traffic profile. I'll kick off the sandbox tests as soon as we have the prompt set.


Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@fintechco.com>, Jane Park <jane.park@fintechco.com>, Procurement <procurement@fintechco.com>

Subject: Re: FinTechCo - Post-demo performance/SLO recap & MAP

Appreciate the fast turnaround, Tom. We're all set on our side for the schedule below. Two small additions before tests: 

- Please send the 1k prompt sample and confirm client chunk size (bytes/tokens). If you prefer a secure upload, I can send a Drive folder or the HubSpot secure file intake.
- For procurement: attached one-page SLO summary (included in slo-checklist.pdf). If Procurement has SLA redlines, send them to me and I'll loop in Legal.

Next steps (confirmed):
- Tom: upload prompts + chunking details by today EOD (FinTechCo)
- Aditya: run sandbox tests Mon 3 May 09:00 PT and share results Tue 4 May
- Rishi: review results and propose production rollout config (autoscale, fallback policy) by Wed 5 May

I'll open a HubSpot activity and share the Drive links after this thread. Thanks everyone - speak soon.
